reason: Conditional probability is a restriction of the normal curve to T > 70, and the hypothesis test is a tail area of the sample-mean curve, so both are clearer as shaded pictures.

scenes.title: Silver badge, given the time is over 70 seconds
scenes.purpose: See that knowing $T>70$ shrinks the sample space to the area above 70, so the silver area is divided by that smaller area.

elements.value: Silver area up to the limit is {area(S)}
Set the limit to 95 and divide: $0.740\div 0.898\approx 0.823$

steps.text: The grey region is everything you know Mira could be in: $T>70$. Its area is $1-0.10156=0.898$, the A1ft for $\mathrm{P}(T>70)$.
The green region is $70<T<95$, the silver area from part (b), about $0.740$. It sits wholly inside the grey region, so the two events are not independent.
The required probability is green area over grey area: $\frac{\mathrm{P}(70<T<95)}{\mathrm{P}(T>70)}$, the M1. Dividing gives $\frac{0.73979}{0.89844}\approx 0.823$, the dM1 and final A1.
Drag the limit to 125: the green fills nearly all of the grey region, so the ratio heads towards 1. Dividing by $0.740$ or multiplying $0.898\times0.740$ would not describe this picture.

guide.what_you_see: The normal density curve for the time $T \sim \mathrm{N}(84, 11^2)$ taken on Level 12, with the region above $T=70$ shaded grey and the silver region from $70$ up to a slider limit shaded green inside it.

legend.meaning: The density curve of $T \sim \mathrm{N}(84, 11^2)$, the first-attempt time in seconds, drawn along the horizontal axis.
The grey region under the curve for $T>70$ (drawn from $70$ to $130$). Its area is $\mathrm{P}(T>70)$, the condition Mira is known to satisfy.
The green region under the curve from $70$ to the slider value $u$. With $u=95$ it is $\mathrm{P}(70<T<95)$, the silver-badge probability from part (b).
The solid vertical line at $T=70$, the gold badge cut-off and the left edge of both shaded regions.
The dashed vertical line at $T=95$, the upper end of the silver range in the question.

interact.do: Drag the slider between $71$ and $125$, first setting it to $95$, then moving it up to $125$.
interact.watch: At $u=95$ the green area reads about $0.740$ against the grey $0.898$, and $0.740\div0.898\approx0.823$. As $u$ rises towards $125$ the green fills nearly all of the grey region, so the ratio of green to grey heads towards $1$.

question_link.text: The grey region is $\mathrm{P}(T>70)$, the smaller sample space once you know Mira missed gold, and its area $1-0.10156=0.898$ is the A1ft. The green region at $u=95$ is $\mathrm{P}(70<T<95)$, and green divided by grey, $\frac{\mathrm{P}(70<T<95)}{\mathrm{P}(T>70)}$, is the M1; carrying out the division to get $0.823$ is the dM1 and A1.

read_off: The label 'Area where $T>70$' gives $\mathrm{P}(T>70)$, which should read about $0.898$. It does not change with the slider, and it is the denominator of the conditional probability.

The label 'Silver area up to the limit' gives $\mathrm{P}(70<T<u)$. At $u=95$ it reads about $0.740$, the part (b) probability and the numerator. For other values of $u$ it is the area up to that limit, not the silver probability.

scenes.title: Is a sample mean of 80.2 unusually low?
scenes.purpose: See the sample mean has standard deviation 2.2, so 80.2 lies far enough into the lower tail to give a p-value below 0.05.

steps.text: Under $\mathrm{H}_0:\mu=84$ against $\mathrm{H}_1:\mu<84$, the sample mean follows a curve centred at 84. The alternative is lower, so only the left tail matters (B1).
The curve is narrow because its standard deviation is $\frac{11}{\sqrt{25}}=2.2$, not 11. Then $z=\frac{80.2-84}{2.2}=-1.727$ (M1).
The shaded tail up to $80.2$ has area about $0.0421$ (A1). The dashed line at about $80.38$ is the critical value for 5%; $80.2$ lies to its left.
Drag the sample mean up towards $81$: the tail grows past $0.05$ and you would keep $\mathrm{H}_0$. At $80.2$ you reject, so there is evidence the mean first-attempt time has decreased (final A1).

guide.what_you_see: The bell-shaped curve of the sample mean $\bar{T}$ for 25 players if the mean time is still $84$ seconds, with the lower tail up to the slider value shaded. A dashed line marks the 5% critical value and a solid line marks $84$.

legend.meaning: The distribution of the sample mean $\bar{T}\sim\mathrm{N}\left(84,\frac{11^2}{25}\right)$ under $\mathrm{H}_0$, with standard deviation $2.2$. It is much narrower than the distribution of a single time.
The shaded lower tail of $g$ from the left edge up to the slider value $m$. Its area is $\mathrm{P}(\bar{T}\leqslant m)$, the p-value when $m=80.2$.
Dashed vertical line at $84-1.645\times2.2\approx 80.38$, the 5% critical value for the lower-tail test.
Solid vertical line at $\mu=84$, the mean under $\mathrm{H}_0$.

interact.do: Drag the sample mean from $76$ to $84$. Start at $80.2$, the observed value, then move it up towards $81$ and back.
interact.watch: The shaded tail grows as $m$ increases. At $m=80.2$ the area is about $0.0421$, which is below $0.05$. The tail area reaches $0.05$ at about $80.38$, where the shaded edge meets the dashed line. By $m=81$ the area is above $0.05$.

question_link.text: The curve $g$ is the sampling distribution of the mean of the 25 new players under $\mathrm{H}_0:\mu=84$, and only the left tail is shaded because $\mathrm{H}_1:\mu<84$ (B1). Its standard deviation of $2.2$ gives $z=\frac{80.2-84}{2.2}=-1.727$ (M1). The shaded area of about $0.0421$ is the p-value, which is less than $0.05$ (A1). The shaded edge at $80.2$ lies to the left of the dashed line, so you reject $\mathrm{H}_0$.

read_off: The label 'Tail area (p-value)' shows the area of $P$, which is $\mathrm{P}(\bar{T}\leqslant m)$. At $m=80.2$ it reads about $0.0421$. If it is below $0.05$ you reject $\mathrm{H}_0$, and if it is above $0.05$ you do not.
